Traditional Mezcal Service for La Noche de Rábanos

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Serves 4-6Prep 10 min

While mezcal itself is a complex spirit crafted by artisans, enjoying it properly is an art form, especially during Oaxaca's vibrant La Noche de Rábanos. This 'recipe' guides you in serving mezcal with its traditional accompaniments, enhancing the festive atmosphere of this unique radish carving festival. It's a moment to savor the rich culture and flavors of Oaxaca.

Ingredients

  • 1 (750 ml) bottle artisanal mezcal (esp. Espadín or Tobalá)
  • 2-3 large oranges, thinly sliced
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) sal de gusano (worm salt) or sal de chapulín (grasshopper salt)
  • 1 small jícama, peeled and cut into sticks (optional)
  • 1 small cucumber, peeled and sliced (optional)
  • Filtered water, for palate cleansing

Method

  1. Choose a high-quality artisanal mezcal. For a traditional experience, look for Espadín, or a more complex varietal like Tobalá or Tepeztate.
  2. Arrange the thinly sliced oranges on a small serving plate. Ensure they are fresh and vibrant.
  3. Place the sal de gusano (or sal de chapulín) in a small, shallow bowl. This savory, spicy salt is a quintessential mezcal accompaniment.
  4. If using, arrange the jícama sticks and cucumber slices on another small plate. These offer a refreshing contrast to the mezcal.
  5. Set out small, traditional mezcal copitas (clay cups) or small tasting glasses for each person.
  6. Provide a pitcher of filtered water, along with small glasses, for palate cleansing between sips.
  7. Pour a small amount of mezcal into each copita, about 1/2 to 1 ounce (15-30 ml).
  8. Instruct guests to first appreciate the aroma of the mezcal, then take a tiny 'kiss' to prepare the palate, followed by small sips, allowing the flavors to develop.
  9. Encourage guests to alternate sips of mezcal with bites of orange dipped in sal de gusano, or a refreshing piece of jícama or cucumber.

Tips

  • Always sip mezcal slowly; it's meant to be savored, not shot. The Oaxacan saying is 'Para todo mal, mezcal, y para todo bien, también' (For every ill, mezcal, and for every good, also).
  • Experiment with different mezcal varietals. Each agave type offers a unique flavor profile, from smoky and earthy to floral and fruity.
  • For a true Oaxacan experience, seek out sal de gusano made with real maguey worms and chiles; its umami depth perfectly complements the mezcal.
